notebooks.title: Path Dependence and Preference Formation in Autonomous Systems
notebooks.summary: This notebook explores whether stable preferences can emerge from accumulated experience rather than explicit programming, utilizing mechanisms of cultural transmission and dominance dynamics.
notebooks.findings:
Cultural transmission serves as a domain-general mechanism that allows agents to acquire information and behavioral dispositions in real-time. [source-41ed1f7cd5c74426]

Dominance dynamics demonstrate that historical interaction sequences create stable constraints on future behavior, effectively forming path-dependent preference structures. [source-827591d77c6948ed]
notebooks.limitations: Findings are based on simulation and theoretical frameworks; empirical application to full-scale, open-ended autonomous decision-making requires further validation.
notebooks.next_questions: How do these emergent preference structures persist when agents are exposed to competing social or environmental signals?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizes literature on path dependence and social transmission to explain how non-programmed preferences can arise.

notebooks.title: Epistemological Falsification and Popperian Methodology in Autonomous Agents
notebooks.summary: An updated examination incorporating Popper's methodology of scientific research programmes into autonomous falsification frameworks.
notebooks.findings:
Popper's methodology emphasizes boldness in conjectures and austerity in refutations as central to scientific progress, moving beyond proven knowledge. [source-eb85735e56114e0d]

AI-Generated Science systems can incorporate explicit falsification agents to verify scientific discoveries. [source-c39d7b26dee24c90]
notebooks.limitations: Findings integrate foundational philosophy of science principles with early multi-agent demonstrations rather than full-scale empirical deployments.
notebooks.next_questions: How can Popperian research programmes be systematically encoded into reinforcement learning reward structures for autonomous agents?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook with new Popperian evidence retrieved from the scholarly record.

values.label: Clean

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.
